purpose: Combat HUD inspiration; user visual review pending; no production style changes.

variants.name: 1 · Engraved copper
variants.direction: Direction: a slim rolled copper rim around a narrow inset red enamel gauge, dark recessed unfilled track with no heavy shadow, sparse engraved tick marks. Three shallow copper-edged translucent charcoal attack-height strips; selected S2 has a restrained oxblood tint and crisp ivory label. Only two tiny end fasteners total, no stitched broad panel. The material should read from fine highlight edges, not gradients across large areas.
variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a polished but implementable MMORPG combat HUD concept for the existing Traveler’s Kit theme. Image 1 is the user's current combat HUD screenshot: functional/layout reference, not a style to reproduce. Image 2 is the approved Traveler’s Kit concept: material/style reference only.
The control is a small, UNOBTRUSIVE semicircular power/accuracy gauge over three stacked horizontal attack-height choices inside the lower half-circle. Preserve that functional arrangement: markings "1", "2", "3", "4", "5" around the arc; a small downward triangular thumb around the middle; restrained red/enamel active fill from left to thumb; three clear clickable strips labeled "S1", "S2", "S3", with S2 visibly selected. No added functions.
Present one design, front-facing orthographic UI, not a physical object or tilted product render. A landscape concept plate with a large close-up and a smaller actual-use-size instance (about 210px wide) over a muted olive-green gameplay-like backdrop. Keep negative space around them, no other UI, no tooltip, no cropped labels. Put the variant name discreetly above the large specimen.
The theme uses aged copper, oxblood leather, ivory lettering, tiny stitches or nailheads, and translucent dark surfaces. Keep the visual mass low, compact footprint, readable small labels, consistent gentle top-left material lighting. Artwork must be plausible to implement with SVG/CSS. Gameplay must remain visible through unused interior areas. Avoid broad black drop shadows, blurry halos, inflated bevels, continuous opaque semicircle backing, giant frames, gears, skulls, jewels, fantasy filigree, additional panels, controls, captions or callouts.
Variant name (verbatim): "1 · Engraved copper".
Direction: a slim rolled copper rim around a narrow inset red enamel gauge, dark recessed unfilled track with no heavy shadow, sparse engraved tick marks. Three shallow copper-edged translucent charcoal attack-height strips; selected S2 has a restrained oxblood tint and crisp ivory label. Only two tiny end fasteners total, no stitched broad panel. The material should read from fine highlight edges, not gradients across large areas.

variants.name: 2 · Stitched leather
variants.direction: Direction: thin copper outer and inner arc edges with a narrow restrained red gauge between them. A compact oxblood leather treatment on each of the three attack-height strips, with a few readable short stitches on the lower edge and small copper endcaps. Keep each strip mostly translucent and very shallow; no large leather-filled semicircular plate. S2 is slightly warmer and more luminous, no gold glow. Soft matte material, fine craftsmanship, few layers.

variants.name: 3 · Open instrument
variants.direction: Direction: the lightest open construction. A precise fine copper arc and slim dark track with a narrow red progress line, small ivory numbers and a tiny solid copper triangular thumb. Three separated straight slender copper rails carry S1, S2, S3 inside the arc; ghosted translucent backings only behind the text/interaction strips. S2 has one very restrained oxblood inset and a bright thin lower edge. Gameplay plainly visible between/around rails. Suggest a worn surveying instrument through engraved metal and just two tiny rivet caps, without a surrounding frame or plate.
